column3: The Hebrew explicitly says “where you saw” and initially addresses one person, then switches to plural “you” for the journey. BSB does not express the seeing clause.
The Hebrew says “in this matter”; BSB interprets the relation as “in spite of all this.”
The Hebrew says “the sound of your words”; BSB simply says “your words.”
The Hebrew says “his sons”; BSB broadens this to “his descendants.”
The Hebrew says “there”; BSB supplies “the land.”
The Hebrew says “plunder” and “today”; BSB uses “captives” and “on that day.” It repeats “they” as the subject of entering and possessing.
The Hebrew name is literally “Sea of Reeds”; BSB uses the traditional “Red Sea.”
The Hebrew says “I am not in your midst” followed by a clause preventing defeat; BSB connects the purpose directly with His being with them.
The Hebrew says “the mouth of the LORD” and separately mentions acting presumptuously and going up; BSB has “command” and combines the actions.
The Hebrew starts with collective singular “the Amorite” and simply says “bees,” without “a swarm.” It says “in Seir,” rather than “from Seir.”
The Hebrew repeats the name of the LORD; BSB uses “He” for the second occurrence.
The Hebrew repeats “days” and “you stayed” in a comparison. BSB supplies “For this reason” and renders the comparison as “a very long time.”
